meta.description: Professor Nagy Habib: hepatobiliary surgeon at Imperial College London since 2003; radiofrequency liver resection and the Habib devices; first clinical trials in gene therapy, stem cells and saRNA for liver disease; founder of EMcision and co-founder of MiNA Therapeutics.

sections.label: The work
sections.statement: Four decades between the operating theatre <t>and the laboratory.</t>
body: A surgeon of the liver, the pancreas and the bile ducts, trained with Henri Bismuth and Thomas Starzl, and Professor of Hepatobiliary Surgery at Imperial College London since 2003. In 1993, the first living-related liver transplant in Africa and the Middle East.

Alongside the operating list, a run of first clinical trials for liver disease: adenovirus and plasmid gene therapy, autologous bone-marrow stem cells, and small activating RNA. And the instruments that came out of the theatre: radiofrequency devices for a near-bloodless liver resection, taken to market by AngioDynamics and Boston Scientific.
<t>[A personal note in Professor Habib’s own words to follow: why the liver, and what keeps the work moving between the theatre, the laboratory and the companies.]</t>

sections.label: Firsts
sections.title: A record <t>of firsts.</t>
sections.lede: Each with its year and the paper that reported it.
items: 1993. The first living-related liver transplant in Africa and the Middle East. International Surgery, 1993.
2001. The first clinical trial of an engineered adenovirus against liver cancer. Human Gene Therapy, 2001.
2002. Liver resection by radiofrequency, sealing the tissue before the cut. Annals of Surgery, 2002.
2006. Patients’ own bone-marrow stem cells for liver insufficiency, among the first such trials in the West. Stem Cells, 2006.
2008. Hydrodynamic gene delivery to a single segment of the human liver. Cancer Gene Therapy, 2008.
2020. The first small activating RNA drug given to patients. Clinical Cancer Research, 2020.

sections.label: The defining chapter
sections.title: A cut that <t>barely bleeds.</t>
sections.body: The liver bleeds when it is cut, and blood loss shapes what follows: transfusions, intensive care, recurrence. The answer from Hammersmith was to seal the tissue with radiofrequency energy before dividing it. The technique was published in 2002; the Habib 4X followed, built with Imperial’s Department of Engineering through EMcision, a spin-out from the college. An endoscopic version, the Habib EndoHPB, took the same energy inside the bile duct to treat tumours that block it.

sections.label: Through MiNA Therapeutics
sections.sub: Co-founded with Robert Habib, its founding Chief Executive since 2013. Small activating RNA raises the activity of a gene instead of silencing it; MTL-CEBPA, designed to restore C/EBP-α in the liver, was the first drug of its kind given to patients, in a phase I trial published in 2020. Professor Habib serves on the company’s Scientific Advisory Board.
